title: [v0.93.1][compiler] Enforce resource limits before semantic validation
summary: Enforce public compiler resource limits before semantic validation can recursively traverse typed document inputs or dependency graphs.
non_goals_inline: No parser fuzzing, broad compiler refactor, Runtime or provider changes, shared binary replacement, main writes, or remediation of other external findings.
dependencies_inline: Planning #12 authorization; Sprint 4 independent review finding ADL-1240-EXT-02; frozen source f75f0d3f9c4df85743638b956f2c2a80f3424f38.
target_files_surfaces_inline: Compiler limit preflight, language dependency-cycle validation traversal, and focused compiler limit regression tests only.
deliverables_inline: Iterative pre-validation structural limit enforcement; stack-safe semantic dependency traversal; focused regressions; independently reviewed PR with required CI.
validation_plan_inline: Focused locked offline adl-compiler limits_and_diagnostics integration test and formatting for touched Rust files; native proof and exact-head independent review. PVF local deterministic contract, bounded CPU/filesystem, no provider calls.
acceptance_criteria_inline: Deep typed inputs and over-limit declared or inline workflows return LimitExceeded before semantic validation; accepted dependency chains use stack-safe validation even within default limits; existing focused diagnostics remain stable.
notes_risks_inline: Preflight must cover every declared workflow because language validation visits unselected declarations. Node preflight alone does not make an accepted default-limit dependency chain safe, so semantic cycle traversal must be iterative or explicitly stack bounded.
